sections.title: Origins & History
sections.text: Hampi, in the Vijayanagara district of Karnataka, is the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, one of the greatest Hindu kingdoms of South India. The city was founded in 1336 by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I and reached its peak under rulers such as Krishnadevaraya in the early 16th century, when it was a vast, wealthy trading centre. In 1565, after the Battle of Talikota, the city was attacked and plundered by a coalition of Deccan sultanates and never regained its prominence.

sections.title: Beauty & Atmosphere
sections.text: The beauty of Hampi is its landscape. Giant golden boulders are piled across the hills, the Tungabhadra River winds through banana and rice fields, and hundreds of temples, pavilions, gateways and markets lie scattered among the rocks. The mix of nature and architecture makes it feel almost unreal at sunrise and sunset, and many travellers climb Matanga Hill for the view.

sections.title: Architecture & Highlights
sections.text: The monuments show the full range of Vijayanagara architecture. The Virupaksha Temple is still active and has a tall gateway tower. The Vittala Temple is famous for its stone chariot, which appears on an Indian banknote, and for its musical pillars. The Hazara Rama Temple has carved scenes from the Ramayana along its walls. The Lotus Mahal, Elephant Stables and Queen's Bath show Indo-Islamic influences in the royal quarter, and the Royal Enclosure has stone platforms and water structures. Giant monolithic statues, such as Ugra Narasimha, add to the sense of scale.

sections.title: Famous For
sections.text: Hampi was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986. It was placed on the endangered list in 1999 and removed in 2006 after measures to protect it. The site is famous as one of the largest open-air ruins in the world and a centre of Kannada and South Indian history.

visitor_tips: Visitors should plan two to three days, wear comfortable shoes and sun protection, and consider hiring bicycles or an autorickshaw.
The cooler months from around October to February are best.
Hospet is the nearest railway town, and Anegundi lies across the river.
Check ticket and access rules with official sources.
